Installation Report

On the date noted above, our team successfully completed the installation of the equipment in accordance with the agreed specifications. This included the mounting of the television, connection of all required cables, and configuration of both audio and video settings.

Inspection and Testing

Following installation, a thorough inspection and testing process was conducted to ensure optimal performance of all components. The following steps were completed:

  1. Visual Inspection: All cables were properly secured, and the installation area was reviewed for any potential safety hazards.

  2. Functionality Test: The television was powered on, and all input sources were tested to confirm proper connectivity and operation.

  3. Audio and Video Quality Check: Sound and picture quality were evaluated to ensure compliance with industry standards.

General Condition of Equipment

All installed equipment is confirmed to be in full working order. No defects or malfunctions were identified at the time of inspection.

Customer Acknowledgment

By signing below, the customer confirms that the installation has been completed to their satisfaction. The customer also acknowledges that all equipment is functioning correctly and assumes responsibility for its ongoing use and care.

Important best practices:
Title/Label is what is shown to the end user on the forms and in the grid.
Code/Value is what is stored in the database and should be unique per Area and must adhere to the specified limitations (e.g. no commas, quotes, or special characters)
Code/Value values should never be changed once any records have been tied to them. You can change the title if needed, but note that it will impact all records that are already tied to that code.
Codes can be set to Inactive, but should not be deleted unless no records have been tied to that code. If disabled, they will be removed from the option list unless you are editing a record with that code.
Codes will be ordere by Place (if populated), then alphabetically by label.

Important best practices:
Title/Label is what is shown to the end user on the forms and in the grid.
Code/Value is what is stored in the database and should be unique per Area and must adhere to the specified limitations (e.g. no commas, quotes, or special characters)
Code/Value values should never be changed once any records have been tied to them. You can change the title if needed, but note that it will impact all records that are already tied to that code.
Codes can be set to Inactive, but should not be deleted unless no records have been tied to that code. If disabled, they will be removed from the option list unless you are editing a record with that code.
Codes will be ordere by Place (if populated), then alphabetically by label.
